name: Hydrocotyle
look_here_first: Flip round leaf to test peltate petiole attachment, then photograph the WHOLE reproductive axis: H. umbellata crowded terminal cluster; H. verticillata small spaced whorls on main axis; H. bonariensis main umbel rays split into secondary axes each with its own whorls. Old H. verticillata var. triradiata = H. bonariensis at Kew, verify voucher before species approval.
shared_traits: Creeping moist-ground/wetland herbs rooting from rhizomes/stolons at nodes. Both current project species have round-to-orbicular leaf blades.
Central underside petiole insertion (peltate), radiating palmate veins and shallow crenate/scalloped margins in H. umbellata and H. verticillata; not all Hydrocotyle worldwide are peltate.
Small white to greenish flowers, with five separate short petals and stamens; flower group is NOT an Asteraceae head.
Dry flattened two-part schizocarp made of mericarps and often faint ribs; not a single solid seed/capsule.
Vegetative similarity requires reproductive-axis scrutiny, ideally with full stalk and 1-mm fruit close-ups.

comparison_matrix.umbellata: Usually a condensed terminal large umbel-like cluster; a few additional tiers possible
comparison_matrix.verticillata: Several clearly separated verticillate whorls on axis; often 2–12 tiers

comparison_matrix.umbellata: Frequently 15–35+ tiny flowers together, roughly 30+ in local UT treatment
comparison_matrix.verticillata: Usually fewer flowers per individual whorl; local var triradiata often 4–8

comparison_matrix.umbellata: Flattened 2-mericarps; base frequently more deeply notched
comparison_matrix.verticillata: Flattened, 2-mericarps; base often more broadly rounded
UT Williamson var triradiata leaves ~21–35 x 24–40 mm

overlap_cautions: Umbellata may produce additional whorls; inspect the whole axis.
Crowded upper whorls of verticillata may appear as a single cluster.
Use fruit only as supporting evidence; leaves alone do not distinguish the species.
Precise verticillata measurements from UT Austin refer to var. triradiata.
CURRENT TAXONOMY WARNING: older H. verticillata var. triradiata names in local floras are assigned to H. bonariensis by Kew POWO; do not silently merge variety claims into accepted H. verticillata.
Inflorescence may branch in H. verticillata; use a full fertile specimen and consider H. bonariensis when terminal rays themselves bear whorls.

lookalikes.separator: Leaf has an open deep notch to petiole, NOT peltate like umbellata; may float on water, blade more boldly lobed.
Peltate leaves but compound/brached inflorescence with secondary whorls/rays, unlike typical simple terminal umbel.
Leaves rounded, scalloped but petiole joins blade at a BASAL NOTCH, not centrally from underneath.
Nonpeltate kidney blades with petiole at basal notch, few-flowered tiny ground-hugging umbels; do not infer Hays nativity.
Petiole joins basal kidney notch, blade mostly ENTIRE, solitary five-lobed green/cream flower and 2-lobed capsule.
Kidney, nonpeltate, smooth margin and solitary small flowers; mature pedicel recurved in fruit.
Opposite toothed leaves and tiny YELLOW composite heads; not peltate.
Opposite leaves, small pale compact button/spike of many flowers raised on stalk, not peltate.

diagnostic_photo_checklist: Large round leaf flipped to show petiole attached inside lower leaf face (both project species).
Whole rooting rhizome plus node roots—not inferred from standing leaf stalks alone.
Complete flowering axes at matched scale; umbellata crowded terminal vs verticillata spaced tiers.
Close flower faces with five petals, and each subcluster pedicels.
Measured mature fruits showing two flattened mericarps, ribbing and base shape.
Leaf base of Dichondra/Centella showing stalk attaching at notch, NOT leaf center.
handoffs: Both species already have canonical learner cards; continue targeted existing-card photo/anatomy improvement only.
Separate worker lanes should not overwrite these user-directed finished-pass records; respect current manifest, current claims and verified photo-source rights.
County BONAP native-zone decisions deferred; do not upgrade approval based on Texas-level distribution.

crew_quick_field_key: 1 · Is petiole attached UNDER leaf inside perimeter? No → look at Dichondra, Centella or H. ranunculoides, not H. umbellata/verticillata.
2 · If round peltate leaf, show main flower stalk from base to tip and count clusters.
3 · One dense many-flowered terminal cluster mostly → H. umbellata (check whole stalk and fruit).
4 · Several separated small whorls along axis → H. verticillata (check subtle crowded/extra tiers).
5 · Branched compound arrangement with secondary rays/whorls → investigate H. bonariensis.
6 · Sterile pennywort or damaged inflorescence → retain Hydrocotyle sp. rather than force an exact name.

taxonomy_exception_20261020.issue: Kew POWO 2026 accepts Hydrocotyle verticillata Thunb., BUT synonymizes Hydrocotyle verticillata var. triradiata (A.Rich.) Fernald with H. bonariensis, while the older local UT Williamson County flora still describes that variety within H. verticillata.
taxonomy_exception_20261020.crew_rule: Do not treat older var. triradiata descriptions or photos, or source-labeled iNaturalist images alone, as a fully verified voucher of accepted H. verticillata. A reproductive voucher or taxonomic expert may be needed for unusual branched stalks.

crew_photo_comparison_activity.title: Dollarweed or whorled pennywort? Look at the whole inflorescence.

umbellata.look_for: Crowded many-flowered terminal white umbel held near round peltate leaf, long flower stalk not in full view.

verticillata.look_for: Separated whorls along flowering/fruiting axis annotated from source-labeled research-grade image.

crew_photo_comparison_activity.critical_warning: Inflorescence structure is a strong genus-comparison clue, NOT species proof in every plant; modern Kew H. bonariensis synonyms include older H. verticillata var. triradiata. Check full reproductive branching, fruit and voucher when needed.
crew_photo_comparison_activity.crew_prompt: If you can only see a round leaf, leave it Hydrocotyle sp. Photograph the whole flowering stalk and leaf underside. Does it have one crowded terminal head or multiple separated small whorls?

three_species_field_key_20261020.photo_key: One dense crowded terminal flower group; whole stalk normally simple
Several small interrupted whorls along main flower axis; can rarely branch; taxon concept caution
COMPOUND umbel, with distinct primary rays each capable of carrying secondary whorls along their length; source-labeled reference images require voucher review

umbellata.visible: crowded flowering umbel; check original photo pixels
